title: Latency bound tests poll at TX-start so min_us==0
description:
CORRECTNESS review of python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py (min_us==0). Distinct from 4i0v, which only fixed the variance-ratio path in test_latency_consistent_across_hops.

Metrics.record_reception records latency as poll_time_us - tx_start_us. BARRIER_SYNC get_rx_result at t=TX-start therefore stores 0us. The consistency test documents this (lines 251-256) and advances 1ms before polling so min_us is a real hop sample.

Every other test still calls get_rx_result immediately after start_transmission with no airtime offset:
- test_three_node_line lines 105-107
- test_five_node_line lines 155-160
- test_latency_under_concurrent_transmissions lines 200-205
- test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay lines 307-308
- test_latency_bounded_with_degraded_signal lines 348-349
- test_sustained_load_latency_bounded lines 381-385
- test_bursty_traffic_latency_bounded lines 431-432

When those tests get deliveries, min_us == max_us == p99_us == 0. Upper-bound asserts (max_us <= HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US, p99_us <= MAX_P99_LATENCY_US, max_us <= CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US) are then tautologies: they cannot fail even if hop latency were unbounded. 4i0v's min_us > 0 assert is not applied outside the consistency test.

Fix: poll after a positive airtime offset (same pattern as the consistency test) and assert min_us > 0 wherever an upper bound is claimed.
close_reason: Hops poll get_rx_result after spec airtime (airtime-1 us, last in-flight us) not at TX-start. Harness elapsed == recorded latency; min_us > 0. Bounds can fail if airtime or injected delay exceeds budget.
